definition_en: the second month of the year, between January and March
core_image: 冬末的雨落在还没醒来的街道上
scene: 二月常常下雨，我们出门都带伞。 February is often rainy, so we take umbrellas when we go out.
sceneCN: 这里 February 是「二月」（第 1 个义项：一年中的第二个月，在一月与三月之间）；句意：二月常常下雨，我们出门都带伞。

senses.title: The second month of the year
senses.definition: the second month of the calendar year, with twenty-eight days in most years
senses.definitionCN: 公历年的第二个月，多数年份有二十八天
senses.example: February is the shortest month.
senses.why: The month is named for an ancient purification festival and still sits at winter's end.
senses.whyCN: 这个月以古老的净化节命名，如今仍站在冬天的末尾。

senses.title: The last stretch of winter
senses.definition: the month seen as the cold season's final stage before spring
senses.definitionCN: 被视为春天来临前寒冷季节最后阶段的月份
senses.example: February days are still short and grey.
senses.exampleCN: 二月的白天仍然又短又灰。
senses.why: Coming last in winter, the month carries the feeling of waiting for warmth.
senses.whyCN: 排在冬天的最后，这个月带着等待温暖的感觉。

senses.title: The month of leap years
senses.definition: the month that gains an extra day in a leap year
senses.definitionCN: 在闰年中会多出一天的月份
senses.example: February has twenty-nine days in a leap year.
senses.exampleCN: 闰年的二月有二十九天。
senses.why: The shortest month is the one chosen to absorb the extra day, so it stands out on calendars.
senses.whyCN: 最短的月份被选来吸收多出的那一天，因此在日历上格外特别。

intro.cn: February 得名于古罗马的净化节 februa。

items.cn: Februarius 意为净化节之月。

items.cn: 这个名字进入法语后写作 fevrier。

items.en: English borrows the month as Februarie.
items.cn: 英语借入这个月名，写作 Februarie。

items.en: The spelling settles as February.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 February。

items.en: February keeps its short length and its leap day.

definition_en: a seat for one person, with a back, or the person who leads a meeting
core_image: 一把有靠背的椅子摆在桌前，等着有人坐下来说话

senses.whyCN: chair 经法语来自希腊语 kathedra「座位」，家具义项至今仍是它最先指的东西。

senses.definition: the person who leads a meeting or organisation
senses.definitionCN: 主持会议或领导组织的人

core_image: 一只手同时抓着电话、笔和一叠纸，桌上还排着待办的事
scene: 办公桌上电话响个不停，手里还攥着一叠没签完的纸。 She is busy with her homework.
sceneCN: 这里 busy 是「忙的」（第 01 个义项）；句意是她忙着做作业。

pos.zh: 形容词：忙的、繁忙的、占线的

senses.title: Having a lot to do
senses.definition: having much work to do, with little free time
senses.example: She is busy with her homework.
senses.why: Busy comes from Old English bisig, 'occupied, diligent', and its centre is a person who cannot put the work down.
senses.whyCN: busy 来自古英语 bisig「专心、操劳」，核心就是一个放不下手里事情的人。

senses.title: Full of activity
senses.definition: full of people or movement, used of places and times
senses.definitionCN: 形容地方或时段人来人往、活动不断
senses.example: They live on a busy street.
senses.exampleCN: 他们住在一条繁忙的街上。
senses.why: A place can be as occupied as a person: if people keep coming and going, the street itself is busy.
senses.whyCN: 地方也能像人一样「闲不下来」：人来人往不断，街道本身就 busy。

senses.title: In use, of a telephone line
senses.definition: already in use, said of a telephone line
senses.definitionCN: 电话线正被使用，打不进去
senses.example: The line is busy.
senses.why: A line that is occupied cannot take another call, so the same word for 'taken up' is used for the telephone.
senses.whyCN: 一条被占用的线接不进别的电话，于是表示「被占着」的同一个词用到了电话上。

senses.title: To keep oneself occupied
senses.definition: to keep oneself occupied with something
senses.example: She busied herself with the dishes.
senses.why: The adjective turned into a verb, so to busy oneself is to make oneself busy on purpose.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转作动词，busy oneself 就是主动让自己忙起来。

definition_en: a large road vehicle that carries many passengers for a fare
core_image: 一辆方方正正的公共汽车停在站牌旁，车门一开人就涌进去
scene: 早晨的站牌下排着长队，车一停大家依次上去。 The children took the bus to school.

senses.title: A large road vehicle for passengers
senses.definition: a large road vehicle that carries many passengers for a fare
senses.definitionCN: 沿道路行驶、收费运送许多乘客的大型车辆
senses.example: The bus stops outside the school.
senses.exampleCN: 公共汽车停在学校外面。
senses.why: Bus is a short form of omnibus, Latin for for all, because the vehicle carries everyone rather than a private party.
senses.whyCN: bus 是 omnibus 的缩略，拉丁语意为「为所有人」，因为这种车谁都能坐，而不是私人包车。

senses.title: To carry people by bus
senses.definition: to transport people by bus
senses.example: They bused the children to the museum.
senses.exampleCN: 他们用大巴把孩子送到博物馆。
senses.why: English often turns a vehicle noun into a verb, so the bus that carries a group also names the act of carrying them.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把交通工具名词直接当动词，于是运送一群人的 bus 也成了「用大巴运送」这个动作。

scene: 书桌上摊着作业本和铅笔，孩子正一行行写字。 They do their homework together.

pos.zh: 助动词：用于疑问与否定

senses.title: To perform an action or task
senses.definition: to carry out an action, job or piece of work
senses.definitionCN: 执行某个动作、活儿或任务
senses.example: They do their homework together.
senses.why: Old English dōn was the general verb for carrying out anything, and it still fills that role when no more specific verb is needed.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 dōn 是表示「执行」的万能动词，在找不到更具体的动词时，它仍旧顶上这个位置。

senses.title: Used to form questions and negatives
senses.definition: used with another verb to form questions, negatives and emphasis
senses.definitionCN: 与实义动词连用，构成疑问、否定或强调
senses.example: Do you like this song?
senses.why: English needed a helper to build questions, and the general verb do was chosen; in this role it carries no meaning of its own.
senses.whyCN: 英语需要一个帮手来构造疑问句，于是选中了万能动词 do；在这个位置上它本身不携带词义。

senses.title: To be enough or acceptable
senses.definition: to be enough for a purpose, or to be acceptable
senses.definitionCN: 足够应付某个用途，或可以接受
senses.example: That will do for now.
senses.why: If a thing "does", it has performed what was asked of it, so do came to mean that something meets the need and no more is required.
senses.whyCN: 一样东西「do」，就是它把要求的事做到了，于是 do 引申为「够用、可以了」，不必再多。

scene: 一片绿色的田野，远处有几座农舍和一条小路。 They walk through the countryside on Sunday.
sceneCN: 这里 countryside 是「乡村」（第 01 个义项）；句意是星期天他们在乡间散步。

senses.title: Land away from towns and cities
senses.definition: the land outside towns and cities, with fields, woods and small villages
senses.definitionCN: 城镇之外、有田野树林和小村庄的地带
senses.example: They walk through the countryside on Sunday.
senses.exampleCN: 星期天他们在乡间散步。
senses.why: Country once meant the land around a town, and side adds the idea of a stretch of ground, so countryside is the open land beyond the built-up area.
senses.whyCN: country 原指城镇周围的土地，side 加上「一片地方」的意思，countryside 就是建成区之外的那片开阔地。

senses.title: The rural scenery as a view
senses.definition: the fields and villages seen as a landscape, especially when it looks beautiful
senses.definitionCN: 把田野村庄当作一片风景来看，尤指好看的时候
senses.example: The countryside looks golden at sunset.
senses.why: People speak of the countryside the way they speak of a picture, because the fields and hedges outside town are something you stop and look at.
senses.whyCN: 人们说 the countryside 时像在说一幅画，因为城外那些田野和树篱正是让人停下来看的景致。

definition_en: a container made of flexible material with an opening at the top
core_image: 一块软布四角收拢，东西都落进同一个兜里
scene: 早市上摊主把新摘的豆角倒进布袋，秤杆还挂着。 The seller filled a bag with beans and handed it over.
sceneCN: 这里 bag 是「有开口的容器」（第 01 个义项）；句意是她用布袋子装米。

derivatives.zh: 由 bag 加 -ful 构成，义为「一袋之量」
由 bag 加 -y 构成，义为「宽松鼓起的」
经由法语来自同一 bag 词，义为「行李」

senses.title: A container open at the top
senses.definition: a container made of paper, cloth or plastic, open at the top
senses.definitionCN: 用纸、布或塑料制成、上端开口的容器
senses.example: She carried the fruit in a paper bag.
senses.exampleCN: 她把水果装在一个纸袋里。
senses.why: Bag probably comes from Old Norse baggi, a pack or bundle, so the container is the oldest sense.
senses.whyCN: bag 很可能来自古诺斯语 baggi「包裹、一捆」，所以「容器」是最早的意思。

senses.title: The amount a bag holds
senses.definition: the amount that a bag holds
senses.definitionCN: 一只袋子所能装下的分量
senses.example: He bought a bag of rice.
senses.why: Once a container is familiar, its name can measure what fills it, so a bag of rice means the quantity inside one bag.
senses.whyCN: 容器一旦常见，它的名字就能计量所装的东西，a bag of rice 指一袋能装下的量。

senses.title: The bag a person carries daily
senses.definition: a handbag or a school bag carried every day
senses.definitionCN: 日常随身携带的手提包或书包
senses.example: She put her keys in her bag.
senses.why: In everyday British English bag often shortens handbag or school bag, the bag a person carries all day.
senses.whyCN: 在日常英式英语里，bag 常用来简称 handbag 或 school bag，也就是随身携带的那只包。

items.en: Bag appears in Middle English, probably from Old Norse baggi; the earlier source is uncertain.
items.cn: bag 见于中古英语，可能来自古诺斯语 baggi；更早来源不确定。

items.en: Old Norse baggi meant a bundle or pack, spread by Norse trade.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 baggi 指一捆或一包，随北欧贸易传播。

items.en: No reliable Indo-European root is agreed; the word may be a loan.
items.cn: 没有公认的可靠印欧词根；这个词可能是借词。

items.en: The noun widened from a pack to handbags and luggage.
items.cn: 现代英语中名词从包裹扩展到提包与行李。

items.en: The verb grew in the nineteenth century and later took the sense of securing.
items.cn: 动词用法在十九世纪发展起来，后来又产生「抢先占取」义。
